description: WTGs must be spaced 0.77 nautical miles east-west and 1.02 nautical miles north-south.
context_quote: The Proposed Action includes the installation of up to 114 WTGs, extending up to 938 feet (286 meters) (height of tip blade) above the sea surface with an east-west spacing of 0.77 nautical miles (1.43 kilometers) and a north-south spacing of 1.02 nautical miles (1.89 kilometers).

description: WTGs must include obstruction aviation lights on the nacelle and tower.
context_quote: Obstruction aviation lights are planned to be placed on the nacelle and tower of each WTG. US Wind expects to install two medium-intensity obstruction aviation lights on top of each nacelle and four low-intensity obstruction lights midway up each tower (approximately 229.7 to 262.5 feet [70 to 80 meters] above mean sea level), as well as a helicopter hoist status light.

description: Offshore export cables must be buried 3.3 to 9.8 feet deep.
context_quote: US Wind plans to bury offshore export cables 3.3 to 9.8 feet (1 to 3 meters) and inter-array cables 3.3 to 6.6 feet (1 to 2 meters) deep, but no more than 13.1 feet (4 meters) deep.

description: No in-water work within Indian River Bay between March 1 and September 30.
context_quote: Based on feedback from DNREC, US Wind will implement the following time of year restrictions to minimize impacts of sediment disturbance, including, no in-water work (e.g.; cable installation, HDDs, dredging) within Indian River Bay between March 1 and September 30, and no HDD activities in the Atlantic to the beach landfall from April 15 through September 15 to avoid impacts to spawning horseshoe crabs.

description: WTGs must not be installed within 1 nautical mile of the traffic separation scheme (TSS) from Delaware Bay.
context_quote: The Proposed Action includes a 1 nautical mile (1.9 kilometer) setback from the traffic separation scheme (TSS) from Delaware Bay which removes 7 of the 121 WTG positions, resulting in a total of 114 WTGs.
